answer_to_question: Both delta questions answered YES, each re-derived by mutating scripts/coverage.py in the working tree and running the real suite, then restoring (sha256 of scripts/coverage.py back to e84216854ee9a13d80ada2beadd3e056190ac95990bad92bf7a206fa351b0f5d, git status shows no unstaged change to either staged file, and git diff --cached still hashes to 75fcbb07). Baseline: ./gradlew -p buildSrc test --tests binjava.CoverageGateTest -> tests=15 skipped=0 failures=0 errors=0; the full buildSrc suite is green too (9 classes, 89 tests, 0 failures). (1) THE UNREACHABILITY CLAIM IS CORRECT and the deletion of 'or not parts[1].strip()' is justified -- the packet's own argument (parts[1] starts non-whitespace) is true but weaker than needed; the decisive argument is the TAIL: line is stripped, parts[1] runs to end of line, so parts[1]'s last character IS line's last character, which strip() guarantees is non-whitespace, so parts[1].strip() is truthy whenever len(parts)==2. I checked the one way that proof could fail -- str.strip()'s whitespace set differing from str.split(None)'s -- exhaustively over all 0x110000 codepoints: the two sets are IDENTICAL (both differences empty), and a brute force over all 3-character whitespace tails built from their union produced 0 reachable inputs with whitespace-only parts[1]. No fixture could reach that clause. Deleting it rather than fabricating a state the code cannot reach is the right call and is not a weakening. (2) THE NEW GUARD'S MUTATIONS ARE SEPARATED. Five mutations, each killed by anExclusionWithoutAReasonIsRefused ALONE: delete the arity guard entirely (IndexError -> exit 1, so startsWith("1") survives but contains("is excluded with no reason") kills it); 'if malformed: return 1' -> pass; 'len(parts) < 2' -> '< 1'; drop the malformed.append (silent skip); and the pre-guard behaviour out[parts[0]]='' (accept with an empty reason) -- that last is the exact regression the guard exists to prevent and the test kills it. The boundary is pinned from BOTH sides: 'len(parts) < 2' -> '< 3' is killed by honoursAnExclusionListedInTheBaseline and anExcludedModuleIsNotCountedAsMeetingTheFloors, so len==2 must be accepted and len==1 must be refused. The doesNotContain("EXCLUDED:") assertion at :291 is the weakest of the three (no single mutation needed it) but it is not inert: it is what separates 'refused' from 'refused and also honoured'. (3) THE RENAME LEAVES NO ASSERTION RESTING ON A DROPPED CLAIM. The body is unchanged and still kills the mutation the old name was earned by: restoring "and not p.startswith('buildSrc/')" in the module comprehension fails buildSrcIsNotExemptFromTheModuleList and nothing else. Both assertions are about LIST MEMBERSHIP (exit 1, and 'buildSrc has compiled classes but no JaCoCo report'), never about regeneration, so the new name is the weaker and TRUE claim rather than a loosened assertion. It also does not assert the remedy line 'Run ./gradlew jacocoTestReport', which is the line M0.44 must change -- so the test pins fail-closed without enshrining the wrong remedy. That is the right seam. (4) NOTHING PREVIOUSLY ASSERTED WAS LOOSENED. Every assertion the round-nine record cited by line is still present and still lethal: I re-ran c.get('BRANCH', (0, 0)) -> (91, 100) and it is still killed by aReportWithNoBranchCounterScoresFullBranchCoverage at :208. Test count went 14 -> 15; no test was deleted. TR7 is closed: M0.42, M0.43 and M0.44 are real rows in the staged backlog (lines 48, 49, 50). Two minor findings below, both surviving mutations, both recorded for backlog rows rather than as changes-requested per the round-ten instruction: neither makes the gate report success while measuring nothing, and neither is in the delta's new behaviour -- TR8 is a pre-existing untested line that the new guard made more consequential, TR9 is an unasserted diagnostic detail.

findings.summary: The blank-line and comment skip in coverage.py's excluded() is unconstrained by any of the 15 tests, and this delta made mutating it dangerous rather than harmless. Verified: "if not line or line.startswith('#'):" -> "if line.startswith('#'):" SURVIVES the whole suite (15 tests, 0 failures), and so does the other half, -> "if not line:". No fixture's baselines/coverage.txt contains a blank line, and only one contains a comment whose content is never asserted on.
findings.failure_scenario: Surviving mutation: drop 'not line or' from coverage.py's skip. Before this round that was merely untidy -- an empty line produced parts == [] and fell through the old len<2 path. The new guard dereferences parts[0]: I ran the mutated script against a baseline of the shape a human writes, '# module  why' / blank line / 'format  M1 lands the SPI', and it died with IndexError: list index out of range at coverage.py's malformed.append((n, parts[0])). That is a Python traceback instead of a diagnostic -- exactly the failure mode aMalformedReportFailsWithAReasonRatherThanATraceback refuses one layer down, and it lands on the one file a human hand-edits. The mirror mutation, dropping startswith('#'), silently turns a comment header into an exclusion for a module named '#'. One fixture kills both: a baseline with a comment line, a blank line and a real entry, asserting the entry is still honoured (exit 0, contains EXCLUDED) and doesNotContain("Traceback"). Not blocking: baselines/ holds only review.txt today, so no committed input reaches it, and the unmutated code is correct.

findings.summary: anExclusionWithoutAReasonIsRefused constrains THAT the gate refuses but not WHICH entry it names. The diagnostic's file:line locator and module name are asserted nowhere; the test reads only the invariant sentence 'is excluded with no reason'.
findings.failure_scenario: Surviving mutation, run and confirmed green at 15 tests / 0 failures: in coverage.py's diagnostic, '% (RED, OFF, BASELINE, n, name)' -> '% (RED, OFF, BASELINE, 0, \'zzz\')'. The gate then prints 'baselines/coverage.txt:0  "zzz" is excluded with no reason' and the suite agrees. The line number and the name are the entire actionable content of a refusal on a file that will hold one row per module: in a thirty-entry baseline the gate would refuse the commit while pointing at a line and a module that do not exist, which makes a correct refusal unfixable. Two assertions close it, using the fixture's own shape (the bare name is on line 2): .contains("coverage.txt:2") and .contains("\"format\"").
